newsitem.title: USA: Health experts offer new stroke treatment strategy.
newsitem.headline: Health experts offer new stroke treatment strategy.

text.p: A new approach to treating strokes, including the use of emergency care similar to that used for heart attacks, could help the half-million Americans who suffer strokes each year, health experts said on Friday.

"We're entering a new era in the treatment of stroke, prompting major changes in medical practice along the entire spectrum of the health care system," said Zach Hall, director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, which hosted a meeting to develop a new treatment plan.

The institute announced the first effective treatment for acute strokes exactly a year ago -- the use of the same kinds of clot-busting drugs that work for some heart attacks -- but without a rapid response to the stroke, such drugs are less effective, Hall said in a statement.

People suffering from acute strokes should get the same kind of fast, time-critical care as heart attack and trauma patients, Dr. Paul Pepe of Allegheny General Hospital in Pittsburgh told the gathering.

The key links in the so-called "chain of recovery" for stroke patients include: fast identification of strokes; quick access to emergency medical assistance via "911" dispatchers; fast transport of patients by emergency vehicle to treatment centers; quick diagnosis and intervention at these centers; specialised treatment and evaluation and appropriate rehabilitation where possible.

Until recently, health professionals had little choice but to respond to the damage caused by stroke, rather than preventing such damage, but now certain strokes can be treated with drugs to minimise long-term disability.
